Langley is the first country artist to be nominated in each of the Big Four categories since Bobbie Gentry in 1968, who was the first artist from any genre to achieve the feat. title: Samsung’s Phone app could start checking if calls from contacts are being spoofed
summary: Use RCS-based caller verification, which first arrived on Pixels in June 2026.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung’s Phone app could soon warn you when a scammer is faking a call from your contacts. The feature uses RCS to verify that the call is indeed coming from the caller your phone says it is from. It does not share the caller’s details with Samsung’s servers, but will require an active internet connection. The feature will not verify calls coming from unknown callers, but only the ones saved in your contacts. In June this year, Google introduced a mechanism to identify potentially harmful spoofed or fake calls on Pixel devices . That way, a scammer using a spoofing tool to make the call appear to come from one of your contacts could be easily discovered. The feature works on RCS, the media-rich texting protocol that allows instant messaging on Google Messages, to match the call’s origin to the contact’s device. At the time of its release on Pixel phones, Google said it plans to expand it to other devices, and we’re seeing signs of that happening now, starting with One UI 9.5 on Samsung Galaxy devices.

title: Bluetooth HDT could finally fix wireless audio quality, but there’s still one big problem

body: News that Bluetooth has officially adopted its new High Data Throughput (HDT) specification should be music to audiophile ears far and wide. And there’s a good chance your future pair of wireless headphones could sound considerably better as a result. If you missed the announcement, Bluetooth HDT extends the capabilities of Bluetooth Low Energy (LE), boosting its maximum physical-layer data rate (PHY, pronounced “fie”) from 2Mbps to a comparatively colossal 7.5Mbps. That’s almost four times the maximum rate of conventional Bluetooth LE, and 2.5 times faster than Bluetooth Enhanced Data Rate (EDR), which tops out at 3Mbps.

title: Android Auto’s music controls are still skipping two songs with one press
summary: One button press, two skipped songs, and no fix in sight.
body: TL;DR Android Auto users are reporting that a single press of their steering-wheel media controls skips two songs instead of one. Initially reported by Toyota RAV4 owners earlier this year, the issue is now being reported with other vehicles and aftermarket stereos. Google support has contacted affected users and escalated recent complaints to the Android Auto team, but there’s no confirmed fix. Steering-wheel buttons are supposed to make controlling music easier while driving, but some Android Auto users are finding that a single press can send their playlists two songs forward or backward. It’s a frustrating problem that has been around for months, and fresh complaints suggest it isn’t going away anytime soon. The issue first gained attention earlier this year , when owners of the 2026 Toyota RAV4 reported that pressing the next or previous button on their steering wheels registered two commands instead of one. The behavior affected multiple music apps, including Spotify and YouTube Music, across wired and wireless connections.
